clue.text: Baby fruit's not right - this is a small vegetable

indicators.note: 'not right' asks for the abbreviation of right, R, to be dropped from the fruit

blocks.note: a chick is a baby bird, and slang for a baby generally
a pear is a fruit; the 's links it to what follows

explanation.surface: Someone comments that a baby's fruit isn't right, and offers a tiny vegetable instead.
explanation.walkthrough: PEAR loses its R to leave PEA, which joins CHICK.
explanation.definitionFit: The chickpea is a small round legume eaten as a vegetable, as in hummus or curries.

clue.text: Its rise and fall leaves members more or less exposed

definitions.text: Its rise and fall leaves members more or less exposed

blocks.note: surface reading: the ups and downs of some institution

blocks.clueFragment: leaves members more or less exposed
blocks.note: setter's reading: the members are legs, shown more or less as fashion raises or lowers a skirt's edge

explanation.walkthrough: Members sound like club or party members exposed by a scandal; here they are limbs, and the rise and fall is fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: The bottom edge of a skirt or dress goes up and down with fashion, showing more or less leg.

clue.text: Family infested with measles, say? Dad's first to come to grief

indicators.note: a thing infested has something inside it, so one word goes within the other
'first' keeps only the opening letter of the word before it

blocks.note: a clan is a family group
measles is an example of an illness producing a rash
the first letter

explanation.surface: A household full of measles, with father the first to fall ill.
explanation.walkthrough: Measles is just one example of what causes spots, hence 'say'.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft that crash-lands comes down in an emergency and is damaged, a literal coming to grief.

clue.text: One who gently touches the line?

blocks.note: first meaning: someone who pats
second meaning: a salesman's or entertainer's glib talk

explanation.walkthrough: A line here is smooth persuasive talk, not a drawn mark, so the sense that seems to go with touching is a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who pats is literally one who pats, and glib rapid talk, a sales pitch, is also called this.

clue.text: Very long time without rain, it seems

blocks.note: first meaning: the idiom for an extremely long period
second meaning: read literally, thirty days of sunshine

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom is split into sun days, as if it described a dry spell.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes an extremely long, indefinite stretch, from the dullness of an old English Sunday.

clue.text: Prison worker's severe blow zero imprisoned, right?

indicators.note: something imprisoned is shut inside, so the zero goes within the word for a severe blow

blocks.note: a gale is a strong wind, a severe blow
zero looks like the letter O
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A question about a prison officer who struck a fierce blow on someone locked up for nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's in the definition stands for 'is': the prison worker is the wordplay that follows. GA(O)LE plus R.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaoler, the British spelling of jailer, is the person who keeps the inmates locked up.

clue.text: Clumsily run girl with swelling to hospital entrance

indicators.note: the entrance is the way in, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: gal is a casual word for a girl
a lump is a swelling
the first letter

explanation.surface: A girl with a painful lump lumbers into the hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is also spelt galumph, the coinage of Lewis Carroll.
explanation.definitionFit: To move in a heavy, ungainly, lumbering way, as a big creature plods along.

clue.text: I certainly will follow the Parisian style of relaxation

blocks.note: le is French for the
taken as written
sure means certainly

explanation.surface: Someone vows to adopt the relaxed French way of living.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Parisian' is the French word for 'the', a common crossword convention; 'will follow' sets the order.
explanation.definitionFit: Leisure is free time spent at ease, away from work, which is a kind of rest.

clue.text: Oboe, say, carrying piece of music, mostly echoed

indicators.note: carrying means holding, so one word is held inside the other
'mostly' means most but not all, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: the oboe is an example of a reed instrument
a sonata is a musical composition

explanation.surface: An oboe playing part of a musical piece filled the hall with sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A sound that resonates rings out and reverberates, the same as when it echoed around a space.

clue.text: Discover what mischief-makers drew?

blocks.note: imps are mischievous little sprites; one of them supplies the word
what someone drew is their art

explanation.surface: A riddle asking you to find out what some naughty children sketched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discover' is used in its old sense of reveal or make known, not find. What imps drew is imp art.
explanation.definitionFit: To discover once meant to disclose or reveal, and to impart is to make information known to someone.

clue.text: Paints and various inks required protective clothing

indicators.note: 'various' suggests the letters can be set out in different ways, so the word inks gets rearranged

blocks.note: oils are oil paints
the four letters rearranged

explanation.surface: An artist working in oils and inks needs to wear something to keep the mess off.
explanation.definitionFit: Oilskins are waterproof garments of oiled cloth worn by sailors and fishermen against wind and spray.

clue.text: Least demanding trial of veracity, roughly speaking

indicators.note: 'speaking' points to how words are pronounced, and 'roughly' warns the match is only near

blocks.note: a test to find whether someone is telling a lie

explanation.surface: A lie detector check described as the least demanding exam, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: A lie test said out loud sounds much like the superlative of light, as in light work.
explanation.definitionFit: Light duties are easy ones, so the superlative form describes whatever task is easiest or puts the smallest burden on you.

clue.text: Total change of policy introduces quiet improvement in the economy

indicators.note: the policy change introduces something, taking it inside itself

blocks.note: a U-turn is a complete reversal of policy
p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: A government's complete about-face brings about a modest economic recovery.
explanation.walkthrough: P goes after the U of U-TURN.
explanation.definitionFit: An upturn is a rise or recovery, used especially of business activity and markets after a slump.

clue.text: Wild man in black repulsed nearly everyone

indicators.note: something repulsed is driven back, so the word is read in the opposite direction
'nearly' means not quite all of it, so the final letter is lost

blocks.note: a football referee traditionally wore black
everyone is all

explanation.surface: A savage figure dressed in black drives back almost the whole crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: Football referees traditionally wore black kit and were nicknamed the men in black, which is the hint the solver needs here.
explanation.definitionFit: Feral describes animals living untamed after escaping domestication, so it means wild.

clue.text: Foremost of French experts state it will stop you looking bad

definitions.text: it will stop you looking bad

indicators.note: 'foremost of' means the very front of the word, its opening letter

blocks.note: the first letter
aces are experts
to aver is to state firmly

explanation.surface: Leading French specialists declare something will spare your blushes.
explanation.definitionFit: A face-saver is an action or excuse that prevents humiliation and preserves dignity.

clue.text: One at font irritated about padre garbling name

indicators.note: 'about' means around, so one word surrounds the rest
garbling mixes up a message, so these letters come out jumbled

blocks.note: informally, something that got to you irritated you
the letters rearranged with the next
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: Someone at a christening gets annoyed when the chaplain mangles the baby's name.
explanation.walkthrough: The font here is the baptismal font in a church, not a typeface.
explanation.definitionFit: A godparent stands at the baptismal basin during a christening and makes promises on the child's behalf.

clue.text: A bold move, cutting through boulder forming obstacle to traffic

indicators.note: a bold move sets letters in motion, so they shift into a new order
cutting through means driving into the middle, so letters sit inside another word

blocks.note: taken as written
the letters rearranged
a boulder is a large rock

explanation.surface: A daring manoeuvre slicing past a big boulder that blocks the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bold move' reads as one idea, but 'move' acts on the word bold alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A road-block is a barrier set up across a street, often by police, to stop vehicles.

clue.text: A tiny measure church headquarters pointlessly introduced after acute remorse

indicators.note: a compass point is a letter such as E, and being pointless means one is dropped

blocks.note: angst is intense anxiety or guilt
Rome is the seat of the Roman Catholic Church

explanation.surface: Remorse leads the Vatican to bring in a small measure, pointlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: The E dropped from ROME is the compass point east.
explanation.definitionFit: An angstrom is a unit of length of one ten-billionth of a metre, used for atoms and light wavelengths.

clue.text: Conservative's yobbish behaviour displaying such vulgarity

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative; the 's means 'has'
a yob is a British lout, and their conduct is rude

explanation.surface: A Tory politician behaves like a lout, showing how coarse he is.
explanation.walkthrough: A yob is British slang for a loutish young man.
explanation.definitionFit: Crudeness is coarse, tasteless behaviour or language, the same thing as vulgarity.

clue.text: A French girl embracing king, with ill-fated consequences

indicators.note: the girl embraces, holding it inside her name

blocks.note: un is French for a
Lucy is a girl's name
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A French girl hugs a monarch, and it ends badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Unlucky means having bad fortune, so an ill-fated outcome is exactly what it describes.

clue.text: Take it with a sprig of green vegetable

blocks.note: 'it' is old slang for sex appeal, abbreviated SA
a sprig is an old word for a youth, a young lad

explanation.surface: Cooking advice: serve something with a little sprig of greenery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sprig' is not foliage but a young man, and 'it' is sex appeal, a crossword stock abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish of leaves such as lettuce eaten raw is a classic plate of greens.

clue.text: A fake doctor endlessly holds it up -- it's water-based

indicators.note: 'endlessly' means without its end, so the final letter goes
holds means keeps inside, so one word goes within the other
in a down entry, 'up' means read from the bottom to the top

blocks.note: taken as written
a quack is a fraudulent medical practitioner
taken as written

explanation.surface: A charlatan doctor is said to hold up something liquid-based.
explanation.walkthrough: A quack is a fake doctor; 'up' reverses only the word it, as this is a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquatic describes plants, animals or sports that live or take place in water.

clue.text: Sanction busting half-achieved is brought to mind

indicators.note: busting means bursting into something, so the word lands inside another
'half' keeps only part of the word, here its second half

blocks.note: the back four letters
to sanction something is to OK it

explanation.surface: Breaking sanctions, only half-successful, is recalled.
explanation.definitionFit: To evoke is to call up a memory or feeling, so evoked means recalled or summoned into the mind.

clue.text: Works out the answer, and thus likes to omit nothing

indicators.note: to omit something is to leave it out, so a letter is taken away

blocks.note: thus means so
likes, strongly, is loves
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A crossword solver figures out the answer, and so enjoys leaving nothing out.
explanation.definitionFit: To solve a problem or puzzle is to work it out and reach the right conclusion.

clue.text: Vote against incorporating very sad, dark colour

indicators.note: incorporating means taking into the body, so one word holds another

blocks.note: a nay is a vote against
V is the abbreviation for very
feeling blue is feeling sad

explanation.surface: A voter opposes something in a mood as gloomy as a dark shade.
explanation.walkthrough: NA(V)Y then BLUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Navy blue is the deep blue-black shade of naval uniforms, so it is a dark colour.

clue.text: First road turns into railway station

indicators.note: a road that turns doubles back, so it is read the other way

blocks.note: the one who finishes first is the victor
the A1 is Britain's longest numbered road, written A-one, read as AI

explanation.surface: Directions: take the first road, which turns into the station approach.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1 is the main road from London to Edinburgh; its 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Victoria is one of London's major railway terminals, serving trains to the south coast and Gatwick.

clue.text: Causing problems in relation to granny, perhaps?

blocks.note: first meaning: tricky, full of difficulties
second meaning: to do with a knot, of which a granny is one kind

explanation.walkthrough: The granny is not a grandmother but the granny knot, a badly tied reef knot.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorny, complicated issue is described as tangled, and the word literally means full of ties like a granny.

clue.text: Heartlessly rough, yet humdrum beat

indicators.note: without a heart, each word loses its middle and keeps only its ends

blocks.note: first and last letters
first and last letters
first and last letters

explanation.surface: A dull, crude drumbeat described without any feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: A beat in music is its regular pulse or pattern of stresses, the same as its tempo pattern.

clue.text: Colleague gives team a boost

blocks.note: a side is a team
a kick is a boost or thrill

explanation.surface: A workmate gives the squad some encouragement.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidekick is a close companion or assistant, a partner who works alongside someone.
